history.dynasty: Manipur kingdom under King Garib Niwaj (Pamheiba); the temple evokes the dispersion of the Ramanandi cult of Hinduism in Manipur, which did not last long after Garib Niwaj's death
history.period: Built 1725 AD - the only temple built during Garib Niwaj's reign (per gosahin); originally brick, later given a cement coating
history.summary: CSV corrections: this temple is in Imphal (Wangkhei, in the Mahabali forest on the banks of the Imphal River), district Imphal East - NOT in Chandel as the CSV states. The Shri Hanuman Thakur Temple, popularly known as the Mahabali Temple, is a Hindu shrine of Lord Hanuman standing among the Mahabali groves on the Imphal River. King Garib Niwaj built it in 1725 AD - the only temple of his reign. Although built with bricks at first, a cement coating was later provided; a mandapa in front has somewhat shadowed the main temple, and the temple pedestal cannot be seen from outside (per gosahin). Lord Hanuman is worshipped here in human form, and the beautiful idol is carved on a big slab of stone (per thisismyindia). Per thisismyindia, the temple conforms to the hut-type of Bengal style: the sanctum cube is raised as a rectangular structure up to the roof, covered with a dome-shaped hemispherical structure; a double lotus in a criss-cross pattern rests at the top of the roof, kalasas are placed over the crown, and above the kalasas a vase holds a pinnacle with Nilchakra. The temple acts as monumental evidence of the Ramanandi cult's dispersion in Manipur. Hanuman Jayanti is the major festival, drawing large numbers of devotees. The temple is easily reached by cab or taxi within Imphal (per gosahin). Identity certainty: high - multiple travel sources agree on the Imphal/Mahabali location and the 1725 Garib Niwaj origin.

town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur in the north-east of India, the historical seat of the Meitei kings. Wangkhei is a locality in Imphal East on the eastern side of the city; the Mahabali forest grove on the banks of the Imphal River gives the temple its popular name, Mahabali Temple.
